Received package and immediately unpacked and plugged the freezer in. Everything worked and it started getting cold right away. Upon further inspection of the seal, I noticed the left side was not dealing properly. At first I thought I just needed to settle so I went back and checked it 30 minutes later, it still would not seal. When I lifted the lid I saw that there was black marks on the white insulation. Once I started looking around the outside casing, it appeared that the freezer had been bounced around like a pinball. All the corners were cracked and damaged, the left side had a considerable dent in the top and bottom and the back right corner also had a big dent in it. With all these defects the lid was crooked and for that reason it would not seal. Even with the freezer working properly, without a seal all it is is scrap metal.

I love this thing! I'm disabled and live in an apartment, so getting out to do laundry is a problem. I was finally able to get an a portable, apartment washer, but having items dry on racks was taking too long and using too much space. I saw this item and decided to give it a try, since it is 'ventless'. What a Godsend!

I remove items from the washer, shake them out, place them on hangers, then hang them inside of this dryer and set the timer. Although ventless, it doesn't heat up my place (I can't tolerate heat!). It's absolutely silent, safe and when it's done, I simply remove the items from the dryer and place them directly into the closet--on the same hangers! No folding, bagging, ironing, etc. This has made my life SO MUCH EASIER! Between this and the Haier washing machine (also highly recommended), I'm in laundry heaven.

I really tried to like it. The concept was good, but. .. it didn't dry my clothes completely, not even the socks on the first cycle (I often let it run for 150 min in the first cycle ). It just randomly dry 94%of one really thin tshirt.

I have done four loads so far. The clothes range from t-shirts (heavy and light weight), jeans, slacks and blouses....as well as underwear. The humidity levels where I live are really high, so I feel that has some affect on how quickly this dries. I have a thermometer in the room (bedroom) so I can see if this device warms the room as it runs.

Putting it together was relatively easy. The only problem was the bottom of the cover....the zipper keeps coming out and opens at the bottom. Also, there is no clear indication on where you put the bottom of the bag. It doesn't 'fit' over the heater part. But in the end, it really didn't seem to matter! I closed the bottom/held it together with a safety pin and just let the bottom rest on the heater. The heat is being blown up, I didn't feel a lot coming out of the bottom while it was on. However, I did subtract a star because the zipper won't stay 'attached' at the bottom and the top, the 'hanger part' you just place in the pole. It doesn't fit snug and 'tilts' if you aren't careful, and comes out. I feel they should have made it screwed in like the bottom poles.

The loads have taken between 2 to 3 hours to dry. They didn't dry 'stiff' and, for the most part, they did dry wrinkle free. The heavy items took longer (of course) to dry. I just checked it at one hour - removed dry items - then again at second hour. I am waiting for the humidity to drop a bit before I try towels/wash cloths in it.
